newsitem.title: INDIA: India I-Sec recommends buy on zero pct 1999 stock.
newsitem.headline: India I-Sec recommends buy on zero pct 1999 stock.

text.p: India's ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) on Tuesday said it was recommending zero percent government stock maturing in 1999 as an excellent buy.
"This bond will provide an excellent holding period yield even in a rising interest rate scenario," I-Sec said in a commentary released on Tuesday.
It called the bond an "excellent buy at 78.15 rupees."
The zero percent 1999, maturing on January 18, 1999, is a two-year bond now offering 12.87 percent semi-annualised yield.
"On a money market basis it yields 14.04 percent, implying a one year forward rate of a whopping 17.84 percent and creating a strong case for price appreciation," the commentary said.
I-Sec said the security was trading at a steep spread of almost 375 basis points (on a money market basis) over the 364-day treasury bill.
"This spread for a one year maturity differential is very high and is likely to narrow providing potential capital appreciation even in the short term," it said.
It also recommended the bond to investors looking at a longer horizon of about one year.

"The holding period return over the next year will primarily be driven by the one year rate prevailing in January 1998... if one year rates remain flat at current levels of 10.30 percent, the holding period yield on zero percent 1999 will be as high as 16.23 percent," I-Sec said.
Even in an increasing interest rate scenario, this security would provide an excellent yield of 13.46 percent, it said.
